approach.method_basis: The Parent generates fresh molecular offspring from its accepted population and fits a count-fingerprint Gaussian process to all accepted scores. A fixed boosted-tree scalar model separately predicts raw scores from the same molecular counts; its output plus the average accepted-reference residual supplies the active search location. The selector adds the original correlated GP residual, keeps eligibility based on the original GP mean, and buys sequential maxima. The earlier raw pair model remains a passive prediction comparator; the complete archive, survivors and breeding feedback stay active.
approach.novelty: Replace the active raw-score tree with a tree that learns the GP errors frozen when earlier molecules were purchased, and add that learned correction to the current GP mean before the existing reference collapse. This tests one GP-based scalar error-correction mechanism. There are no evaluated same-Parent siblings in the frozen brief. The related chronological-weight sibling learns one coefficient between two complete predictors; this intervention instead learns a feature-dependent error function. Its benefit is untested, and neither the Parent's algebraic consistency nor the sibling's endpoint gain supplies that benefit.

method_change.previous_method: Active fixed unary count tree fitted to accepted raw labels, followed by a uniform accepted-reference intercept; retained GP supplies correlated residual and original-mean eligibility.
method_change.proposed_method: Active fixed unary count tree fitted to immutable prior-paid GP errors, added to the current GP mean as one scalar potential before the same uniform accepted-reference intercept.
method_change.rationale: Code Parent n-a53bc2587706 has correct global potential arithmetic but worse raw-unit error than GP in all fifteen cells. Changing the supervised target and base function is the frozen substantive obstacle intervention. It is one joint component change; no whole-method replacement, GP residual change, generator change or separate component effect is proposed.

hypothesis: One joint target/base-function/readout intervention: at allocation t train the inherited fixed-capacity count tree h_t once on every optimizer purchase i from completed earlier batches, with immutable target e_i=y_i-g_at_purchase_i. Exclude supplied initials and all current or future feedback; with no eligible history h_t is identically zero. Do not recompute e_i after refitting the GP. The unchanged raw-label count GP supplies g_current_t at both accepted references and fresh pool points. Define G_t(x)=g_current_t(x)+h_t(x) and D_t(i,x)=G_t(x)-G_t(x_i). Active raw-unit location is L_t(x)=G_t(x)+(1/n_t)sum_{accepted i}[y_i-G_t(x_i)]. Thus a feature-conditional prospective-error correction changes the active mean while one scalar retains self/swap/cycle consistency and the uniform all-reference collapse. Prediction: candidate-varying correction produces real paid departures and complete same-paid raw-unit MSE is strictly below both passive original raw-y scalar and passive GP with the same reference-intercept operation. GP addition, error supervision and reference readout are inseparable here; no component mediation or separate contribution is claimed.

finding_summary.headline: Honest GP-error correction worsened observed predictions; the interrupted final batch leaves the full test inconclusive
finding_summary.insights: The observed failure is useful because it separates an operational error learner from a useful correction. Purchase-time errors were label-honest, every available prior row entered the next fit, scalar consistency and reference collapse held, and the correction had substantial influence on paid choices. The borrowed original-input error-estimation element therefore operated under the declared chronological adaptation. Its added correction increased average prediction overstatement from 0.01549 to 0.07338, and centered error also increased. A positive error-alignment term accounts for 0.003685 of the 0.011589 MSE increase over matched GP; the correction’s squared magnitude accounts for the rest. Honest historical GP errors thus failed to predict a helpful correction for the current GP on this evolving selected stream. A correction model that conditions on the current posterior state, or a consumer that requires prospective evidence before allowing a learned correction to affect selection, addresses the diagnosed limitation; neither was tested here. The molecular evidence also shows stronger local family reuse: typed/generic scaffold counts fall from 2,017/1,328 to 1,568/870 on matched observed prefixes, while fragment-excluded within-batch similarity rises from 0.7224 to 0.7506. The same similarity direction holds on complete seeds. This supports a separate limitation in obtaining coherent core/linker alternatives, which a structurally different proposal operator could address. Frequent unusual heteroatom-halogen edits and unresolved stereochemistry further limit what high molecular scores imply about chemistry. These associations do not identify a chemical cause of the endpoint losses. The result rules out an inert correction or missing local exposure as the explanation for the observed adverse predictions, narrows this particular target/base/readout intervention, and leaves the complete-panel effect and the broader scalar-potential approach unresolved.
finding_summary.results: The correction executed and changed the search, but its observed predictions were worse than both registered controls. All 419 available nonempty error-tree fits reproduced from their saved models;15 initial fits correctly used zero correction. The 4,340 observed purchases have active mean squared error 0.0198252, versus 0.0110506 for the original raw-score scalar and 0.00823598 for the GP with the same reference-intercept readout. Every one of 14 completed task sessions is worse than both controls; the interrupted session’s 280-purchase prefix is also worse. The direction remains adverse on the 2,900 purchases from the two complete seeds and on 2,165 observed late purchases. The correction changes 413 of 434 purchase sets relative to matched GP and produces 1,915 purchases outside that comparator’s set. Pair ordering is 65.28%, versus 62.50% for the original scalar and 66.79% for matched GP. Completed seeds score 0.574212 and 0.543095, giving mean 0.558654 versus the matched Parent’s 0.585603 and mean paired loss 0.026950;five of ten task endpoints improve and five worsen. Seed 2 ended at the allocation time limit after four complete tasks and 280 purchases in its final task. Its final ten predictions/labels, final task endpoint and seed macro are absent. Therefore the registered 4,350-purchase falsifier and complete three-seed score target are unevaluable, even though the available sessions provide clear adverse predictive results.

molecular.headline: Aromatic ring families with frequent N/O-halogen edits, tighter local scaffold reuse and unresolved stereochemistry
molecular.overall_character: Source node n-efdfc053d389, code Parent n-a53bc2587706, Research in Depth profile epoch 1, batch size 10, issued Search seeds 0/1/2. Seeds 0/1 have complete evaluator summaries; seed 2 ended at the allocation time limit and has incomplete evaluation. Chemistry totals use all 4,340 observed Child optimizer purchases, excluding 150 supplied initial records; the observed-prefix Parent comparison contains 4,340 purchases, while its complete published stream contains 4,350. All fifteen Child and fifteen authoritative published Parent trajectories were read. These describe accepted, scored purchases, not the unevaluated pools or rejected candidates. Four Child tasks contain 900 accepted records each; the remaining task contains 890, because seed 2 stops at evaluation 290 rather than 300. All trajectory paths exist. The missing file is the seed-2 evaluator summary; its execution receipt has exit code 143 and status retryable, and its run log records Slurm step 5238136.79 cancelled due to time limit. This is an ended, failed execution, not successful completion and not evidence that the candidate caused the termination. The frozen comparison marks both child_complete and paired_complete false, with matched seeds 0/1 only. Its Child mean 0.5586535727931246 and paired delta -0.02694957566189099 describe those complete seeds, not the full issued panel. No seed-2 endpoint or missing molecule is imputed. The output consists mainly of fused or linked heteroaromatic systems, carbonyl-rich nitrogen rings, and aromatic groups attached to saturated amines. The frozen string ring-closure rates lie between 0.9954 and 0.9989, and aromatic-token rates between 0.9920 and 0.9977. These rates mean presence in a SMILES, not fractions of atoms. RDKit detects aromatic atoms in 4,321 of 4,340 optimizer purchases, with medians of four rings and fifteen aromatic atoms. The represented chemistry is diverse enough to rule out total ring or scaffold collapse, but local reuse is stronger than in the Parent. There are 1,568 typed and 870 generic scaffolds, versus 2,017 and 1,328 in the matched observed Parent prefix. Pair-count-weighted within-cell count-Tanimoto after excluding <=6-heavy-atom fragments is 0.656569 versus 0.620985; within ten-purchase batches it is 0.750583 versus 0.722379. Restricting both nodes to the completed seeds gives 2,900 purchases each and batch similarity 0.751145 versus 0.708172, so the direction is not created by the partial seed alone. Child heavy-atom size spans 1–86, median 31, versus 2–120, median 32, for the observed-prefix Parent. The <=5/<=6/>=50/>50 tails contain 14/15/186/162 versus 14/16/440/431 purchases. These aggregate reductions are uneven: in the completed seeds, >=50-heavy-atom counts are 158 versus 159 overall, but 72 versus 22 late. The all-observed late cohort contains 2,165 optimizer purchases versus 2,165 Parent-prefix purchases (the full Parent has 2,175); its <=6/>=50 counts are 3/83 versus 2/173, typed/generic scaffold counts 719/384 versus 918/569, and fragment-excluded batch similarity 0.756439 versus 0.740072. Source-defined full/late per-cell denominators and both tail conventions are retained in the audits. There are 907 N–halogen-bearing, 464 O–halogen-bearing, 18 S–halogen-bearing and 219 O–O-bearing Child purchases, versus 434, 181, 170 and 111 in the observed-prefix Parent. Conventional medicinal motifs coexist with these unusual environments, large repeated assemblies and intricate ring fusions, supporting questionable synthetic plausibility rather than a blanket claim that every graph is impossible. Carbon-centred two-double-bond flags occur in 99 purchases, including 87 with cyclic instances; sulfur-centred flags occur in 170 and are kept separate from carbon cumulenes. No assigned tetrahedral centre or specified double-bond stereochemistry occurs; 2,595 molecules carry 5,457 unassigned tetrahedral centres. Only one molecule has formal charges, in a charge-separated nitrogen motif, so explicit charge-state exploration is extremely limited. Neutral amines can still ionize; neither this count nor the amine-like SMARTS measures pKa. Descriptors use the Parent report definitions and RDKit 2023.09.6: canonical typed and generic Murcko scaffolds (including empty acyclic scaffolds), radius-2 chirality-aware 2048-bin Morgan counts and generalized dot-product Tanimoto, comparing pairs only within task/seed cells or original batches. Late means optimizer ordinals 146–290, truncated to observed coverage. Top/bottom subsets contain the fixed 87 recorded purchases per task with seed/evaluation tie-breaking. These are descriptive selected-stream associations, not independent replicates or measured synthesis, stability, toxicity, biological utility, component contribution, or evidence of mechanism activation. method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.
